name: The returned exiles who married strange wives
charge: Mingling the holy seed with the peoples of the lands
summary: Ezra was told that the people, priests, and Levites had taken wives of the Canaanites, Hittites, Ammonites, Moabites, and Egyptians, and that the princes and rulers had been chief in the trespass. He rent his garment and sat astonished until the evening sacrifice. A generation later Nehemiah found children who could not speak the Jews' language.
offense: The returned people, including priests and Levites, had joined themselves in marriage to the peoples whose abominations Ezra named. The princes and rulers were chief in the trespass (Ezra 9:1-2). Deuteronomy had warned against the marriages it forbade because they would turn Israel's children from following the Lord to serving other gods (Deuteronomy 7:3-4). Ezra's grief measured the offense against the mercy already received. God had punished them less than their iniquities deserved and given a remnant deliverance. To return to the forbidden alliances after that revival was to disregard both the command and the lesson of captivity (Ezra 9:13-15).
judgment: The congregation wept and covenanted to put away the strange wives and the children born of them. The matter was examined at appointed times with the elders and judges, beginning in the tenth month and ending by the first day of the first month. Priests found guilty gave their hands to the separation and offered a ram for their trespass (Ezra 10:2-19). Later Nehemiah confronted renewed offenses and recalled Solomon, whom outlandish women had caused to sin. He drove away the priestly descendant allied by marriage to Sanballat (Nehemiah 13:23-29). The leaders' position did not exempt them from the covenant obligations they were responsible to uphold.

verses.text: Now when these things were done, the princes came to me, saying, The people of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites, have not separated themselves from the people of the lands, doing according to their abominations, even of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.

For they have taken of their daughters for themselves, and for their sons: so that the holy seed have mingled themselves with the people of those lands: yea, the hand of the princes and rulers hath been chief in this trespass.
And when I heard this thing, I rent my garment and my mantle, and plucked off the hair of my head and of my beard, and sat down astonied.
And now, O our God, what shall we say after this? for we have forsaken thy commandments,

Which thou hast commanded by thy servants the prophets, saying, The land, unto which ye go to possess it, is an unclean land with the filthiness of the people of the lands, with their abominations, which have filled it from one end to another with their uncleanness.

Now therefore give not your daughters unto their sons, neither take their daughters unto your sons, nor seek their peace or their wealth for ever: that ye may be strong, and eat the good of the land, and leave it for an inheritance to your children for ever.

And after all that is come upon us for our evil deeds, and for our great trespass, seeing that thou our God hast punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and hast given us such deliverance as this;

Should we again break thy commandments, and join in affinity with the people of these abominations? wouldest not thou be angry with us till thou hadst consumed us, so that there should be no remnant nor escaping?

And Shechaniah the son of Jehiel, one of the sons of Elam, answered and said unto Ezra, We have trespassed against our God, and have taken strange wives of the people of the land: yet now there is hope in Israel concerning this thing.

Now therefore let us make a covenant with our God to put away all the wives, and such as are born of them, according to the counsel of my lord, and of those that tremble at the commandment of our God; and let it be done according to the law.
Arise; for this matter belongeth unto thee: we also will be with thee: be of good courage, and do it.
Then arose Ezra, and made the chief priests, the Levites, and all Israel, to swear that they should do according to this word. And they sware.
And Ezra the priest stood up, and said unto them, Ye have transgressed, and have taken strange wives, to increase the trespass of Israel.
Now therefore make confession unto the Lord God of your fathers, and do his pleasure: and separate yourselves from the people of the land, and from the strange wives.
Then all the congregation answered and said with a loud voice, As thou hast said, so must we do.

And the children of the captivity did so. And Ezra the priest, with certain chief of the fathers, after the house of their fathers, and all of them by their names, were separated, and sat down in the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter.
And they made an end with all the men that had taken strange wives by the first day of the first month.
And among the sons of the priests there were found that had taken strange wives: namely, of the sons of Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and his brethren; Maaseiah, and Eliezer, and Jarib, and Gedaliah.
And they gave their hands that they would put away their wives; and being guilty, they offered a ram of the flock for their trespass.
In those days also saw I Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab:
And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language, but according to the language of each people.

And I contended with them, and cursed them, and smote certain of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, saying, Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons, nor take their daughters unto your sons, or for yourselves.

Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? yet among many nations was there no king like him, who was beloved of his God, and God made him king over all Israel: nevertheless even him did outlandish women cause to sin.
Shall we then hearken unto you to do all this great evil, to transgress against our God in marrying strange wives?
And one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite: therefore I chased him from me.

The nation of Israel, the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles to wit, of the Canaanites, Hittites, Pheresites, Jebusites, and the Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites.

For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land; and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity.
And as soon as I had heard these things, I rent my clothes, and the holy garment, and pulled off the hair from off my head and beard, and sat me down sad and very heavy.
So Esdras arose up, and said unto them, Ye have transgressed the law in marrying strange wives, thereby to increase the sins of Israel.
And now by confessing give glory unto the Lord God of our fathers,
And do his will, and separate yourselves from the heathen of the land, and from the strange women.
Then cried the whole multitude, and said with a loud voice, Like as thou hast spoken, so will we do.
Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.
For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.

Judah hath dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah hath profaned the holiness of the Lord which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god.
The Lord will cut off the man that doeth this, the master and the scholar, out of the tabernacles of Jacob, and him that offereth an offering unto the Lord of hosts.

entries.commentary: The princes come to Ezra reporting that the people of Israel, the priests, and the Levites have not separated themselves from the people of the lands, doing after their abominations, the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites. The sin is interracial marriage with the nations, taking their daughters for themselves and their sons, so that the holy seed mingled itself with the people of those lands. It was not only the common people but the Levites, the leaders, that were chief in this trespass. -

When Ezra hears this thing he rends his garment and his mantle, plucks off the hair of his head and beard, and sits down astonished, in distress that the people did this after the Most High showed mercy to bring them out of Babylon. Then everyone that trembled at the words of the God of Israel assembles to him because of the transgression of those that had been carried away, and he sits astonished until the evening sacrifice.

At the evening sacrifice Ezra rises from his heaviness, and having rent his garment and mantle, falls upon his knees and spreads out his hands unto the Lord his God. He says he is ashamed and blushes to lift up his face, for their iniquities are increased over their head and their trespass is grown up unto the heavens. Since the days of the fathers they have been in a great trespass unto this day. For their iniquities they, their kings, and their priests have been delivered into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, and to spoil. The nation is privy to all the captivities it came from, Egypt, Assyria, and Babylon, and knows why it went, yet does the same sins.

Now for a little space grace has been showed from the Lord to leave a remnant to escape and to give them a nail in his holy place, that the Most High may lighten their eyes and give a little reviving in their bondage. Though they were bondmen the Most High has not forsaken them but extended mercy in the sight of the kings of Persia, to give a reviving to set up the house of God and give them a wall in Jerusalem. This is the very leeway that let them come back to the land.

Ezra asks what they shall say after this, for they have forsaken the commandments. It is like a parent giving you something good and you turning and doing something to make him feel wrong for giving it. The commandment given by the prophets said the land they go to possess is an unclean land, filled from one end to another with the filthiness and abominations of the people of the lands. Therefore they were not to give their sons or take their daughters, nor seek their peace or wealth, that they might be strong, eat the good of the land, and leave it for an inheritance to their children forever. This command is reiterated all the way back to the time of Moses.

After all that has come upon them for their evil deeds, and seeing the Most High has punished their iniquities less than they deserve and given such deliverance, Ezra asks should they again break the commandments and join in affinity with the people of these abominations. Would not the Most High be angry until he had consumed them so there should be no remnant left. Oh Lord God of Israel, thou art righteous, for they remain yet escaped as it is this day. They stand before the Most High in their trespass, for they cannot stand before him because of it. Even though the Levites and Israel committed this sin, the Most High still showed them mercy and let them stay in the land.

When Ezra had prayed and confessed, weeping and casting himself down before the house of God, a very great congregation of men, women, and children assembles to him, for the people wept very sore. Shechaniah the son of Jehiel answers and says they have trespassed against their God in taking strange wives of the people of the land, yet there is hope in Israel concerning this thing. He counsels to make a covenant to put away all the wives and the children born of them, according to the counsel of those that tremble at the commandment, and to do it according to the law. This time meant putting away those particular wives and children; it does not mean an Israelite today with a child by another nation must put away the child.

Then Ezra rises and makes the chief priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear to do according to this word, and they swear, the same way an oath was made to keep the commandments. Ezra rises from before the house of God and goes into the chamber of Johanan, and eats no bread nor drinks water, for he mourns because of the transgression of them that had been carried away.

Proclamation is made throughout Judah and Jerusalem to all the children of the captivity that they should gather themselves to Jerusalem. Whosoever would not come within three days, according to the counsel of the princes and elders, would have all his substance forfeited and himself separated from the congregation of those that had been carried away.

All the men of Judah and Benjamin gather to Jerusalem within three days, in the ninth month on the twentieth day, and sit in the street of the house of God trembling because of this matter and the great rain. Ezra the priest stands and says they have transgressed and taken strange wives to increase the trespass of Israel. Now they are to make confession unto the Lord God of their fathers, do his pleasure, and separate themselves from the people of the land and from the strange wives. Doing his pleasure today is the same, separating from unclean people.

The congregation answers with a loud voice, As thou hast said, so must we do, but the people are many and it is a time of much rain, and they are not able to stand outside, neither is the work of one or two days. They ask that the rulers stand for the congregation, and that all who have taken strange wives come at appointed times with the elders and judges of every city, until the fierce wrath of God is turned from them. The fierce wrath is the judgment, and the reference to rain is why they came in portions. Only Jonathan and Jahaziah were employed about this matter, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them, so the sin was dealt with in orderly parts.

The children of the captivity do so; Ezra and certain chief of the fathers, separated by name, sit down on the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter. The leaders and those who did righteously and had not taken other nations sit and judge the matter, for one who is himself in the sin cannot judge it. They make an end with all the men that had taken strange wives by the first day of the first month.

Among the sons of the priests found to have taken strange wives were sons of Jeshua, and they gave their hands to put away their wives, offering a ram of the flock for their trespass, being guilty. The chapter names the Levites, singers, porters, and the men of Israel by their families who had taken strange wives, a long roll of those who had transgressed in this thing. All these had taken strange wives, and some of them had wives by whom they had children, so that some put away only the wives and some the wives and children born of them. -

On that day they read in the books of Moses and found written that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever, because they met not Israel with bread and water but hired Balaam against them to curse them, and the Most High turned the curse into a blessing. When the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude. The reading of the law produced immediate obedience, cutting off what the law said to cut off. -

Eliashib the priest, having oversight of the chambers of the house of God, was allied to Tobiah and had prepared him a great chamber where the offerings, tithes, and vessels had formerly been laid. Nehemiah was away in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon, and when he returned and understood the evil, he cast all Tobiah's household stuff out of the chamber, cleansed the chambers, and brought back the vessels of the house of God with the meat offering and the frankincense.

Nehemiah found that the portions of the Levites had not been given, so the Levites and singers had fled every one to his field, and he contended with the rulers and set the Levites back in their place. He made treasurers over the treasuries, faithful men, to distribute unto their brethren, and prayed, Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God.

Nehemiah saw men in Judah treading wine presses on the Sabbath, bringing in sheaves, lading asses, and bringing wine, grapes, and figs into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, and men of Tyre selling fish and all manner of ware on the Sabbath. He contended with the nobles of Judah and asked what evil thing this was to profane the Sabbath day, reminding them that their fathers did the same and the Most High brought this evil upon the city, and now they brought more wrath upon Israel. Buying and selling on the Sabbath is breaking the commandment. -

When the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the Sabbath, Nehemiah commanded them shut and set his servants at the gates so no burden would be brought in on the Sabbath, and the merchants lodged outside Jerusalem once or twice. He testified against them and warned that if they came again he would lay hands on them, and from that time they came no more on the Sabbath. This laying on of hands is not a blessing but a serious warning, and the merchants knew he was not joking. He then commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves and keep the gates to sanctify the Sabbath day.

Nehemiah saw Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak the Jews' language, but according to the language of each people. Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law. Nehemiah contended with them, cursed them, smote certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear not to give or take daughters in marriage with those nations, reminding them that Solomon himself, though beloved of his God, was caused to sin by outlandish women. -

One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite, so Nehemiah chased him away because he had defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites. Thus Nehemiah cleansed the people from all strangers, appointed the wards of the priests and Levites every one in his business, and provided for the wood offering and the firstfruits, closing the book with the prayer, Remember me, O my God, for good. This is the book of records, and to see it as history rather than religion is to understand who these people are. -

After these things, when Artaxerxes the king of the Persians reigned, came Esdras, of the line of Aaron the chief priest. This Esdras went up from Babylon, as a scribe, being very ready in the law of Moses, that was given by the God of Israel. The king did honour him: for he found grace in his sight in all his requests. Esdras had very great skill, so that he omitted nothing of the law and commandments of the Lord, but taught all Israel the ordinances and judgments.

The commission written from Artaxerxes gave order that such of the nation of the Jews, and of the priests and Levites, as were willing should go with Esdras unto Jerusalem. They were to look unto the affairs of Judea and Jerusalem, agreeably to that which is in the law of the Lord, and to carry the gifts unto the Lord of Israel to Jerusalem. Whatsoever Esdras the priest and reader of the law of the most high God should send for, the keepers of the treasuries in Syria and Phenice should give it him with speed. Let all things be performed after the law of God diligently unto the most high God, that wrath come not upon the kingdom of the king and his sons. No tax nor any other imposition was to be required of the priests, Levites, holy singers, porters, ministers of the temple, or any that have doings in this temple. Thou, Esdras, according to the wisdom of God, ordain judges and justices, that they may judge in all Syria and Phenice: all those that know the law of thy God thou shalt teach, and those that know it not.

Blessed be the only Lord God of my fathers, who hath put these things into the heart of the king, to glorify his house that is in Jerusalem. Therefore was I encouraged by the help of the Lord my God, and gathered together men of Israel to go up with me.

These are the chief, according to their families and several dignities, that went up with Esdras from Babylon in the reign of king Artaxerxes, counted family by family with the number of men. They gathered together at the river called Theras, where they pitched their tents three days, and Esdras surveyed them. When he found there none of the priests and Levites, he sent unto the principal men and learned, that they should send such men as might execute the priest's office in the house of the Lord. By the mighty hand of the Lord they brought unto them skilful men of the sons of Moli the son of Levi, the son of Israel, and of the ministers of the temple whom David had ordained.

There Esdras vowed a fast unto the young men before the Lord, to desire of him a prosperous journey both for them and their children and their cattle. I was ashamed to ask the king footmen and horsemen and conduct for safeguard against our adversaries; for we had said unto the king, that the power of the Lord our God should be with them that seek him, to support them in all ways. Then I separated twelve of the chief of the priests, and weighed them the gold, and the silver, and the holy vessels of the house of our Lord, which the king and his council and the princes and all Israel had given. Ye are holy unto the Lord, and the vessels are holy, and the gold and the silver is a vow unto the Lord of our fathers: watch ye, and keep them till ye deliver them to the chief of the priests and Levites at Jerusalem.

From the river Theras we departed the twelfth day of the first month, and came to Jerusalem by the mighty hand of our Lord, which was with us. From the beginning of our journey the Lord delivered us from every enemy, and so we came to Jerusalem. When we had been there three days, the gold and silver that was weighed was delivered in the house of our Lord on the fourth day, all by number and weight, and the whole weight of them was written up the same hour. They that were come out of the captivity offered sacrifice unto the Lord God of Israel, even twelve bullocks for all Israel, fourscore and sixteen rams, threescore and twelve lambs, and twelve goats for a peace offering.

The rulers came unto Esdras and said, The nation of Israel, the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles. For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land; and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity. As soon as I had heard these things, I rent my clothes and the holy garment, and pulled off the hair from off my head and beard, and sat me down sad and very heavy. Rising up from the fast with my clothes and the holy garment rent, and bowing my knees, and stretching forth my hands unto the Lord, I said, O Lord, I am confounded and ashamed before thy face. For our sins are multiplied above our heads, and our ignorances have reached up unto heaven, for ever since the time of our fathers we have been and are in great sin, even unto this day.

In some measure hath mercy been shewed unto us from thee, O Lord, that there should be left us a root and a name in the place of thy sanctuary, and to give us food in the time of our servitude. When we were in bondage we were not forsaken of our Lord, but he made us gracious before the kings of Persia, so that they gave us food, and honoured the temple of our Lord, and raised up the desolate Sion. We have transgressed thy commandments, which thou gavest by the hand of thy servants the prophets, saying, The land which ye enter into to possess as an heritage is a land polluted with the pollutions of the strangers of the land. Therefore now shall ye not join your daughters unto their sons, neither shall ye take their daughters unto your sons; and ye shall never seek to have peace with them, that ye may be strong, and eat the good things of the land, and leave the inheritance of the land unto your children for evermore. All that is befallen is done unto us for our wicked works and great sins; but thou, O Lord, didst make our sins light, and didst give unto us such a root: yet we have turned back again to transgress thy law, and to mingle ourselves with the uncleanness of the nations of the land.

As Esdras in his prayer made his confession, weeping, and lying flat upon the ground before the temple, there gathered unto him from Jerusalem a very great multitude of men and women and children, and there was great weeping among the multitude. Then Jechonias the son of Jeelus, one of the sons of Israel, called out and said, O Esdras, we have sinned against the Lord God, we have married strange women of the nations of the land. Let us make an oath to the Lord, that we will put away all our wives, which we have taken of the heathen, with their children, like as thou hast decreed, and as many as do obey the law of the Lord. Arise, and put in execution: for to thee doth this matter appertain, and we will be with thee: do valiantly. So Esdras arose, and took an oath of the chief of the priests and Levites of all Israel to do after these things; and so they sware. --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Esdras, rising from the court of the temple, went to the chamber of Joanan the son of Eliasib, and remained there, and did eat no meat nor drink water, mourning for the great iniquities of the multitude. There was a proclamation in all Jewry and Jerusalem to all them that were of the captivity, that they should be gathered together at Jerusalem. In three days were all they of the tribe of Judah and Benjamin gathered together at Jerusalem, the twentieth day of the ninth month; and all the multitude sat trembling in the broad court of the temple because of the present foul weather. Esdras arose up and said unto them, Ye have transgressed the law in marrying strange wives, thereby to increase the sins of Israel. Now by confessing give glory unto the Lord God of our fathers, and do his will, and separate yourselves from the heathen of the land, and from the strange women.

The whole multitude cried and said with a loud voice, Like as thou hast spoken, so will we do. But forasmuch as the people are many, and it is foul weather, and this is not a work of a day or two, let the rulers of the multitude stay, and let all them of our habitations that have strange wives come at the time appointed, with the rulers and judges of every place, till we turn away the wrath of the Lord from us for this matter. Esdras the priest chose unto him the principal men of their families, all by name; and in the first day of the tenth month they sat together to examine the matter, and their cause was brought to an end in the first day of the first month.

Of the priests, the Levites, the holy singers, the porters, and of Israel, the names of those that had taken strange wives are set down family by family. They gave their hands to put away their wives, and to offer rams to make reconcilement for their errors. All these had taken strange wives, and they put them away with their children.

The priests and the Levites, and they that were of Israel, dwelt in Jerusalem and in the country, in the first day of the seventh month. The whole multitude came together with one accord into the broad place of the holy porch toward the east, and spake unto Esdras the priest and reader, that he would bring the law of Moses, that was given of the Lord God of Israel. Esdras the chief priest brought the law unto the whole multitude, from man to woman, and to all the priests, to hear the law in the first day of the seventh month, and he read in the broad court before the holy porch from morning unto midday. Esdras stood upon a pulpit of wood, which was made for that purpose, and there stood up by him the men appointed on his right hand and on his left. When he opened the law, they stood all straight up. So Esdras blessed the Lord God most High, the God of hosts, Almighty; and all the people answered, Amen: and lifting up their hands they fell to the ground, and worshipped the Lord.

The Levites taught the law of the Lord, making them withal to understand it. Then spake Attharates unto Esdras the chief priest and reader, and to the Levites that taught the multitude, even to all, saying, This day is holy unto the Lord; for they all wept when they heard the law. Go then, and eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send part to them that have nothing; for this day is holy unto the Lord: and be not sorrowful; for the Lord will bring you to honour. They went their way, every one to eat and drink, and make merry, and to give part to them that had nothing, and to make great cheer; because they understood the words wherein they were instructed, and for the which they had been assembled. --- Topics: [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The seven nations cast out before Israel, the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, greater and mightier than Israel, are Hamitic nations. Thou shalt smite them and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them. Since the days of old the Most High has never been about the love-of-the-world gospel; throw that doctrine in the trash. This is why they do not want you reading the old covenant: verses like this correct the miseducation received through Christianity, and the mind begins to correct itself as you read.

Neither shalt thou make marriages with them: the Most High forbids marrying outside the nation. The seed of the fathers today is found among the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Indians, who make up the twelve tribes of Israel; a spouse may come from any of the twelve tribes, but from within the tribes only. Going outside your nation for a husband or wife is despising your brethren in your heart. Whom you marry is the greatest commitment you make in this life; if you truly loved your people, you would choose one of your own people to become aged together with. They will turn away thy son from following me: the nations are strangers to the Most High and cannot come into this covenant, so they draw the Israelite spouse off to religions that accept everything. Christianity accepts that union, and that is how they turn you away from your God.
Thus shall ye deal with them: destroy their altars, break down their images, cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire. Nothing of their worship was to be spared or adopted.

For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: this is one of the most uplifting scriptures in the book, and it should be etched into your children's minds from the moment they begin to read, until it is implanted into their spirit. The mind controls the body: what goes into the mind comes out through the body, so a people that knows it is holy and special above all people walks and carries itself differently. Being chosen above all people keeps you out of the affairs of this world, their fashions, their hairstyles, their trends and challenges, and keeping up with the Joneses; you cannot flip-flop with every new wave and still carry the speciality the Most High put on you.

The Lord did not choose Israel for their number, for ye were the fewest of all people: only threescore and ten souls came out of the loins of Jacob when Israel first went down, as Genesis records, some places reading seventy and some counting seventy-five. But because the Lord loved you: the Most High needs no other reason, he simply loved us, and we should never apologize for that. He kept the oath sworn unto the fathers and redeemed Israel out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; Israel came out from under Rameses.

Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations, and repayeth them that hate him to their face. This is the same teaching as the new testament: loving the Most High is keeping his commandments, and refusing his commandments shows him with your actions that you hate him, and then judgment comes. From the jump it has always been the same: love God, keep the commandments; nothing changed between the covenants.

If ye hearken to these judgments and keep and do them, the Lord keeps the covenant and the mercy: he will love thee, bless thee, and multiply thee, blessing the fruit of thy womb, thy land, thy corn, wine, oil, kine, and sheep, blessed above all people, which goes right back to verse 6. The Lord will take away from thee all sickness and put none of the evil diseases of Egypt upon thee, but will lay them upon all them that hate thee. That still reigns true today: keep the commandments and the Most High will keep you from the diseases of modern-day Egypt, and if you do catch something, he will revive you and bring you back to your health.

Thou shalt consume all the people which the Lord thy God shall deliver thee; thine eye shall have no pity upon them, neither shalt thou serve their gods, for that will be a snare unto thee. Those days are coming back when Christ returns.

If thou shalt say in thine heart, these nations are more than I: fear them not, but remember what the Lord did unto Pharaoh and unto all Egypt, the signs, the wonders, the mighty hand and the stretched out arm; so shall he do unto all the people of whom thou art afraid. The Lord will send the hornet among them until even those that hide themselves are destroyed, and he will put out those nations before thee by little and little, lest the beasts of the field increase upon thee. He shall deliver their kings into thine hand, and thou shalt destroy their name from under heaven. There is no way to read [Deuteronomy 7](/bible/deuteronomy/7) and still say God loves everybody; that idea is being drunk on Christianity, not reading the book.

The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: desire not the silver or gold that is on them, lest thou be snared therein, for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God. Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it. Bring it up to today: the Jesus pieces, the crosses, the ankhs, and the rosary beads wrapped around the neck and rubbed in prayer make the wearer an abomination and a cursed thing just like the idol. The main abomination we bring into our house is the Christmas tree of Jeremiah 10: the tree cut down, fastened with nails and hammers, and decked with silver and with gold, whether cut from the forest or bought as a fake tree from the store.

lawsResolved.text: We are not to intermarry with those who practice idolatry.
We are not to marry unbelievers.
We are not to marry those of other races.
We are exhorted to acknowledge our transgressions and iniquity and confess them to God.
Confessing of iniquities and turning from them required before God will give mercy and restore His blessings to a people.
Priests to be of an unpolluted genealogy.

text.text: Now when these things were done, the princes came to me, saying, The people of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites, have not separated themselves from the people of the lands, doing according to their abominations, even of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.

For they have taken of their daughters for themselves, and for their sons: so that the holy seed have mingled themselves with the people of those lands: yea, the hand of the princes and rulers hath been chief in this trespass.
And when I heard this thing, I rent my garment and my mantle, and plucked off the hair of my head and of my beard, and sat down astonied.
And now, O our God, what shall we say after this? for we have forsaken thy commandments,

Which thou hast commanded by thy servants the prophets, saying, The land, unto which ye go to possess it, is an unclean land with the filthiness of the people of the lands, with their abominations, which have filled it from one end to another with their uncleanness.

Now therefore give not your daughters unto their sons, neither take their daughters unto your sons, nor seek their peace or their wealth for ever: that ye may be strong, and eat the good of the land, and leave it for an inheritance to your children for ever.

And after all that is come upon us for our evil deeds, and for our great trespass, seeing that thou our God hast punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and hast given us such deliverance as this;

Should we again break thy commandments, and join in affinity with the people of these abominations? wouldest not thou be angry with us till thou hadst consumed us, so that there should be no remnant nor escaping?

And Shechaniah the son of Jehiel, one of the sons of Elam, answered and said unto Ezra, We have trespassed against our God, and have taken strange wives of the people of the land: yet now there is hope in Israel concerning this thing.

Now therefore let us make a covenant with our God to put away all the wives, and such as are born of them, according to the counsel of my lord, and of those that tremble at the commandment of our God; and let it be done according to the law.
Arise; for this matter belongeth unto thee: we also will be with thee: be of good courage, and do it.
Then arose Ezra, and made the chief priests, the Levites, and all Israel, to swear that they should do according to this word. And they sware.
And Ezra the priest stood up, and said unto them, Ye have transgressed, and have taken strange wives, to increase the trespass of Israel.
Now therefore make confession unto the Lord God of your fathers, and do his pleasure: and separate yourselves from the people of the land, and from the strange wives.
Then all the congregation answered and said with a loud voice, As thou hast said, so must we do.

And the children of the captivity did so. And Ezra the priest, with certain chief of the fathers, after the house of their fathers, and all of them by their names, were separated, and sat down in the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter.
And they made an end with all the men that had taken strange wives by the first day of the first month.
And among the sons of the priests there were found that had taken strange wives: namely, of the sons of Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and his brethren; Maaseiah, and Eliezer, and Jarib, and Gedaliah.
And they gave their hands that they would put away their wives; and being guilty, they offered a ram of the flock for their trespass.
In those days also saw I Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab:
And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language, but according to the language of each people.

And I contended with them, and cursed them, and smote certain of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, saying, Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons, nor take their daughters unto your sons, or for yourselves.

Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? yet among many nations was there no king like him, who was beloved of his God, and God made him king over all Israel: nevertheless even him did outlandish women cause to sin.
Shall we then hearken unto you to do all this great evil, to transgress against our God in marrying strange wives?
And one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite: therefore I chased him from me.

The nation of Israel, the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles to wit, of the Canaanites, Hittites, Pheresites, Jebusites, and the Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites.

For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land; and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity.
And as soon as I had heard these things, I rent my clothes, and the holy garment, and pulled off the hair from off my head and beard, and sat me down sad and very heavy.
So Esdras arose up, and said unto them, Ye have transgressed the law in marrying strange wives, thereby to increase the sins of Israel.
And now by confessing give glory unto the Lord God of our fathers,
And do his will, and separate yourselves from the heathen of the land, and from the strange women.
Then cried the whole multitude, and said with a loud voice, Like as thou hast spoken, so will we do.
Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.
For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.

Judah hath dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah hath profaned the holiness of the Lord which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god.
The Lord will cut off the man that doeth this, the master and the scholar, out of the tabernacles of Jacob, and him that offereth an offering unto the Lord of hosts.
